name: Discovery
question: Does a real problem exist, and who has it?

gate.name: Problem-solution fit
asks: Is the problem real, and frequent or painful enough that people already try to solve it?
Who has it, named well enough to find more of them?
Does a solution fit the problem well enough to test it with those people?

evidence.statement: A problem record with evidence from the people who have it
An ideal customer profile that names who has the problem
Interviews with people who have the problem

weights.note: Unvalidated priors, ours: how much each function's open decisions count when decisions are ranked across functions in this phase. They sum to 1. The decision queue ranks with them (packages/naive/src/engine/decision-queue.ts, EE-127).

strategy.why: The problem and who has it is a strategic question before it is a product one

products.why: The solution hypothesis is shaped alongside the problem

marketing-and-sales.why: Talking to the people who have the problem is the main source of evidence

supply-chain.why: Nothing is bought or made yet

service-delivery.why: Concierge delivery may test a solution, rarely

customer-service.why: Early contacts are kept, but there are no customers to serve

human-capital.why: The founding team is set; hiring waits

it.why: A few tools, chosen cheaply and reversibly

finance.why: Runway bounds how long discovery can last

risk-and-compliance.why: Only blocking legal questions matter now

external-relationships.why: Advisers and early backers can open doors to people with the problem

capabilities.why: How the founder learns and records what was learned
